sanskrit: atha yeṣām adharmajño rājā bhavati nāstikaḥ na te sukhaṃ prabudhyante na sukhaṃ prasvapanti ca
english: Now those whose king is ignorant of dharma and a denier of the sacred order—they neither wake in comfort nor sleep in peace.

sanskrit: sadā bhavanti codvignās tasya duścaritair narāḥ yogakṣemā hi bahavo rāṣṭraṃ nāsyāviśanti tat
english: The people are forever distressed by his misdeeds; and many who would have brought security and prosperity refuse to enter his realm.

sanskrit: atha yeṣāṃ punaḥ prājño rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ sukhaṃ te pratibudhyante susukhaṃ prasvapanti ca
english: But those whose king is wise and righteous—they wake in happiness and sleep in deep contentment.

sanskrit: tasya rājñaḥ śubhair āryaiḥ karmabhir nirvṛtāḥ prajāḥ yogakṣemeṇa vṛṣṭyā ca vivardhante svakarmabhiḥ
english: Contented by that king's auspicious and noble deeds, his subjects flourish through their own labors, through prosperity and through the rains.

sanskrit: sa kulīnaḥ sa puruṣaḥ sa bandhuḥ sa ca puṇyakṛt sa dātā sa ca vikrānto yo dadāti vasuṃdharām
english: He is well-born, he is a true man, he is a kinsman, he is a doer of merit, he is a giver and he is valorous—the one who gives away the earth.

sanskrit: ādityā iva dīpyante tejasā bhuvi mānavāḥ dadanti vasudhāṃ sphītāṃ ye vedaviduṣi dvije
english: Like the Ādityas, those mortals blaze with splendor upon the earth who bestow rich land upon a brāhmaṇa learned in the Veda.

sanskrit: yathā bījāni rohanti prakīrṇāni mahītale tathā kāmāḥ prarohanti bhūmidānasamārjitāḥ
english: As seeds scattered upon the ground spring up, so do desires sprout forth when they are won by the gift of land.

sanskrit: ādityo varuṇo viṣṇur brahmā somo hutāśanaḥ śūlapāṇiś ca bhagavān pratinandanti bhūmidam
english: Āditya, Varuṇa, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Soma, the fire-eater Agni, and the blessed Lord who bears the trident—all rejoice in the giver of land.

sanskrit: bhūmau jāyanti puruṣā bhūmau niṣṭhāṃ vrajanti ca caturvidho hi loko 'yaṃ yo 'yaṃ bhūmiguṇātmakaḥ
english: Upon the earth men are born, and upon the earth they come to their end; for this fourfold world is constituted of the qualities of the earth.

sanskrit: eṣā mātā pitā caiva jagataḥ pṛthivīpate nānayā sadṛśaṃ bhūtaṃ kiṃ cid asti janādhipa
english: She is the mother and the father of the world, O lord of the earth; there exists no being equal to her, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam bṛhaspateś ca saṃvādam indrasya ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: And on this matter they recount an ancient tale, the dialogue between Bṛhaspati and Indra, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: iṣṭvā kratuśatenātha mahatā dakṣiṇāvatā maghavā vāgvidāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ papracchedaṃ bṛhaspatim
english: Having sacrificed with a hundred great rites richly endowed with priestly fees, Maghavat questioned Bṛhaspati, foremost of those skilled in speech, on this very matter.

sanskrit: bhagavan kena dānena svargataḥ sukham edhate yad akṣayaṃ mahārghaṃ ca tad brūhi vadatāṃ vara
english: O blessed one, by which gift does a man who has gone to heaven thrive in happiness? Tell me that gift which is imperishable and of great worth, O best of speakers.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa surendreṇa tato devapurohitaḥ bṛhaspatir mahātejāḥ pratyuvāca śatakratum
english: Thus addressed by the lord of the gods, the priest of the celestials, the mightily resplendent Bṛhaspati, replied to him of the hundred sacrifices.

sanskrit: suvarṇadānaṃ godānaṃ bhūmidānaṃ ca vṛtrahan dadad etān mahāprājñaḥ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: The gift of gold, the gift of cattle, and the gift of land, O slayer of Vṛtra—the man of great wisdom who bestows these is released from all his sins.

sanskrit: na bhūmidānād devendra paraṃ kiṃ cid iti prabho viśiṣṭam iti manyāmi yathā prāhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: There is nothing higher than the gift of land, O lord of the gods, O master; I hold it to be the most excellent, even as the wise have declared.

sanskrit: ye śūrā nihatā yuddhe svaryātā dānagṛddhinaḥ sarve te vibudhaśreṣṭha nātikrāmanti bhūmidam
english: Those heroes slain in battle who, eager for giving, have gone to heaven—not one of them, O best of the gods, surpasses the giver of land.

sanskrit: bhartur niḥśreyase yuktās tyaktātmāno raṇe hatāḥ brahmalokagatāḥ śūrā nātikrāmanti bhūmidam
english: The heroes devoted to their lord's supreme good, who lay down their lives and are slain in battle and attain the world of Brahmā—even they do not surpass the giver of land.

sanskrit: pañca pūrvādipuruṣāḥ ṣaṭ ca ye vasudhāṃ gatāḥ ekādaśa dadad bhūmiṃ paritrātīha mānavaḥ
english: Five forefathers and six who have gone before—the man who gives land delivers all eleven of his line here in this world.

sanskrit: ratnopakīrṇāṃ vasudhāṃ yo dadāti puraṃdara sa muktaḥ sarvakaluṣaiḥ svargaloke mahīyate
english: He who gives away land strewn with jewels, O Puraṃdara, is freed from all his impurities and is honored in the world of heaven.

sanskrit: mahīṃ sphītāṃ dadad rājā sarvakāmaguṇānvitām rājādhirājo bhavati tad dhi dānam anuttamam
english: A king who gives away a flourishing land endowed with all that the heart desires becomes a king of kings; that indeed is the gift unsurpassed.

sanskrit: sarvakāmasamāyuktāṃ kāśyapīṃ yaḥ prayacchati sarvabhūtāni manyante māṃ dadātīti vāsava
english: He who bestows the earth of Kaśyapa, furnished with every object of desire—all beings think, 'It is to me that he gives,' O Vāsava.

sanskrit: sarvakāmadughāṃ dhenuṃ sarvakāmapurogamām dadāti yaḥ sahasrākṣa sa svargaṃ yāti mānavaḥ
english: The mortal who gives a cow that yields every wish and grants every desire, O thousand-eyed one, goes to heaven.

sanskrit: madhusarpiḥpravāhinyaḥ payodadhivahās tathā saritas tarpayantīha surendra vasudhāpradam
english: Rivers that flow with honey and clarified butter, and that bear milk and curds, refresh here, O lord of the gods, the giver of land.

sanskrit: bhūmipradānān nṛpatir mucyate rājakilbiṣāt na hi bhūmipradānena dānam anyad viśiṣyate
english: By the gift of land a king is freed from the guilt that clings to kingship; for no other gift surpasses the gift of land.

sanskrit: dadāti yaḥ samudrāntāṃ pṛthivīṃ śastranirjitām taṃ janāḥ kathayantīha yāvad dharati gaur iyam
english: He who gives away the earth bounded by the oceans, won by the sword—men tell of him here for as long as this earth shall endure.

sanskrit: puṇyām ṛddharasāṃ bhūmiṃ yo dadāti puraṃdara na tasya lokāḥ kṣīyante bhūmidānaguṇārjitāḥ
english: He who gives a holy land rich in sap, O Puraṃdara—the worlds he has won by the merit of the gift of land never wane for him.

sanskrit: sarvathā pārthiveneha satataṃ bhūtim icchatā bhūr deyā vidhivac chakra pātre sukham abhīpsatā
english: By every means should a ruler who ever desires prosperity, who longs for happiness, O Śakra, give land according to the prescribed rite to a worthy recipient.

sanskrit: api kṛtvā naraḥ pāpaṃ bhūmiṃ dattvā dvijātaye samutsṛjati tat pāpaṃ jīrṇāṃ tvacam ivoragaḥ
english: Even a man who has committed a sin, by giving land to a twice-born, casts off that sin as a serpent casts off its worn-out skin.

sanskrit: sāgarān saritaḥ śailān kānanāni ca sarvaśaḥ sarvam etan naraḥ śakra dadāti vasudhāṃ dadat
english: Oceans, rivers, mountains, and forests in their entirety—all this a man gives, O Śakra, when he gives away the earth.

sanskrit: taḍāgāny udapānāni srotāṃsi ca sarāṃsi ca snehān sarvarasāṃś caiva dadāti vasudhāṃ dadat
english: Ponds and wells, streams and lakes, oils and every kind of sap—all these he gives when he gives away the earth.

sanskrit: oṣadhīḥ kṣīrasaṃpannā nagān puṣpaphalānvitān kānanopalaśailāṃś ca dadāti vasudhāṃ dadat
english: Herbs abounding in milky sap, trees laden with flowers and fruit, and forests, stones, and crags—all these he gives when he gives away the earth.

sanskrit: agniṣṭomaprabhṛtibhir iṣṭvā ca svāptadakṣiṇaiḥ na tat phalam avāpnoti bhūmidānād yad aśnute
english: Though one sacrifice with the Agniṣṭoma and other rites, complete with their proper priestly fees, he does not attain the fruit that he enjoys from the gift of land.

sanskrit: dātā daśānugṛhṇāti daśa hanti tathā kṣipan pūrvadattāṃ haran bhūmiṃ narakāyopagacchati
english: The giver favors ten generations; he who reviles a gift destroys ten; and he who takes back land once given goes down to hell.

sanskrit: na dadāti pratiśrutya dattvā vā harate tu yaḥ sa baddho vāruṇaiḥ pāśais tapyate mṛtyuśāsanāt
english: He who, having promised, does not give, or who takes back what he has given, is bound in the nooses of Varuṇa and tormented by the decree of death.

sanskrit: āhitāgniṃ sadāyajñaṃ kṛśabhṛtyaṃ priyātithim ye bharanti dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ nopasarpanti te yamam
english: Those who support a brāhmaṇa of the highest order—one who has kindled the sacred fire, ever offers sacrifice, keeps but scant retinue, and loves his guests—do not come near Yama.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇeṣv ṛṇabhūtaṃ syāt pārthivasya puraṃdara itareṣāṃ tu varṇānāṃ tārayet kṛśadurbalān
english: It should be regarded as a debt owed by the king to the brāhmaṇas, O Puraṃdara; but of the other castes too he should rescue the lean and the feeble.

sanskrit: nācchindyāt sparśitāṃ bhūmiṃ pareṇa tridaśādhipa brāhmaṇāya suraśreṣṭha kṛśabhṛtyāya kaś cana
english: Let no one wrest away land once made over by another, O lord of the thirty gods, to a brāhmaṇa of scant means, O best of the celestials.

sanskrit: athāśru patitaṃ teṣāṃ dīnānām avasīdatām brāhmaṇānāṃ hṛte kṣetre hanyāt tripuruṣaṃ kulam
english: And the tears that fall from those wretched, sinking brāhmaṇas when their field is seized destroy three generations of the despoiler's line.

sanskrit: bhūmipālaṃ cyutaṃ rāṣṭrād yas tu saṃsthāpayet punaḥ tasya vāsaḥ sahasrākṣa nākapṛṣṭhe mahīyate
english: But he who restores once more a ruler fallen from his realm—his dwelling, O thousand-eyed one, is honored upon the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: ikṣubhiḥ saṃtatāṃ bhūmiṃ yavagodhūmasaṃkulām gośvavāhanasaṃpūrṇāṃ bāhuvīryasamārjitām
english: Land covered over with sugarcane, thick with barley and wheat, abounding in cattle, horses, and beasts of burden, won by the strength of his own arm—

sanskrit: nidhigarbhāṃ dadad bhūmiṃ sarvaratnaparicchadām akṣayāṃl labhate lokān bhūmisatraṃ hi tasya tat
english: —land whose womb holds treasures and which is adorned with every jewel: the man who gives it attains imperishable worlds, for that is to him a very sacrifice of land.

sanskrit: vidhūya kaluṣaṃ sarvaṃ virajāḥ saṃmataḥ satām loke mahīyate sadbhir yo dadāti vasuṃdharām
english: Having shaken off all his impurity, cleansed of passion and esteemed by the good, he who gives away the earth is honored in the world by the virtuous.

sanskrit: yathāpsu patitaḥ śakra tailabindur visarpati tathā bhūmikṛtaṃ dānaṃ sasye sasye visarpati
english: As a drop of oil fallen upon water spreads, O Śakra, so does a gift made in land spread out in crop after crop.

sanskrit: ye raṇāgre mahīpālāḥ śūrāḥ samitiśobhanāḥ vadhyante 'bhimukhāḥ śakra brahmalokaṃ vrajanti te
english: Those kings, heroes resplendent in the assembly of battle, who are slain facing the foe at the front of combat, O Śakra—they go to the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: nṛtyagītaparā nāryo divyamālyavibhūṣitāḥ upatiṣṭhanti devendra sadā bhūmipradaṃ divi
english: Women given to dance and song, adorned with celestial garlands, attend forever upon the giver of land in heaven, O lord of the gods.

sanskrit: modate ca sukhaṃ svarge devagandharvapūjitaḥ yo dadāti mahīṃ samyag vidhineha dvijātaye
english: He who duly, by the prescribed rite, gives land here to a twice-born rejoices in happiness in heaven, honored by gods and gandharvas.

sanskrit: śatam apsarasaś caiva divyamālyavibhūṣitāḥ upatiṣṭhanti devendra sadā bhūmipradaṃ naram
english: A hundred apsarases, adorned with celestial garlands, attend forever upon the man who is a giver of land, O lord of the gods.

sanskrit: śaṅkhaṃ bhadrāsanaṃ chatraṃ varāśvā varavāraṇāḥ bhūmipradānāt puṣpāṇi hiraṇyanicayās tathā
english: The conch, the throne of state, the parasol, fine horses and noble elephants, and heaps of gold—these are the blossoms that spring from the gift of land.

sanskrit: ājñā sadāpratihatā jayaśabdo bhavaty atha bhūmidānasya puṣpāṇi phalaṃ svargaḥ puraṃdara
english: Command forever unopposed and the cry of victory besides—these are the flowers of the gift of land; its fruit is heaven, O Puraṃdara.

sanskrit: hiraṇyapuṣpāś cauṣadhyaḥ kuśakāñcanaśāḍvalāḥ amṛtaprasavāṃ bhūmiṃ prāpnoti puruṣo dadat
english: Herbs with blossoms of gold, and lawns of kuśa grass and gold—the man who gives land attains a land that brings forth ambrosia.

sanskrit: nāsti bhūmisamaṃ dānaṃ nāsti mātṛsamo guruḥ nāsti satyasamo dharmo nāsti dānasamo nidhiḥ
english: There is no gift like the gift of land, no elder like a mother, no dharma like truth, and no treasure like giving.

sanskrit: etad āṅgirasāc chrutvā vāsavo vasudhām imām vasuratnasamākīrṇāṃ dadāv āṅgirase tadā
english: Having heard this from the son of Aṅgiras, Vāsava then gave to that son of Aṅgiras this very earth strewn with wealth and jewels.

sanskrit: ya imaṃ śrāvayec chrāddhe bhūmidānasya saṃstavam na tasya rakṣasāṃ bhāgo nāsurāṇāṃ bhavaty uta
english: He who recites this hymn in praise of the gift of land at a śrāddha rite—no portion of his offering falls to the rākṣasas or to the asuras.

sanskrit: akṣayaṃ ca bhaved dattaṃ pitṛbhyas tan na saṃśayaḥ tasmāc chrāddheṣv idaṃ vipro bhuñjataḥ śrāvayed dvijān
english: And what is given to the ancestors becomes imperishable—of this there is no doubt; therefore at śrāddhas let a brāhmaṇa recite this to the twice-born as they dine.

sanskrit: ity etat sarvadānānāṃ śreṣṭham uktaṃ tavānagha mayā bharataśārdūla kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi
english: Thus have I declared to you, O sinless one, that which is the foremost of all gifts, O tiger of the Bhāratas; what more do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kāni dānāni loke 'smin dātukāmo mahīpatiḥ guṇādhikebhyo viprebhyo dadyād bharatasattama
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What gifts in this world should a king desirous of giving bestow upon brāhmaṇas of surpassing merit, O best of the Bhāratas?

sanskrit: kena tuṣyanti te sadyas tuṣṭāḥ kiṃ pradiśanty uta śaṃsa me tan mahābāho phalaṃ puṇyakṛtaṃ mahat
english: By what are they at once made content, and what, when content, do they grant in return? Tell me this, O mighty-armed one—the great and holy fruit of such merit.

sanskrit: dattaṃ kiṃ phalavad rājann iha loke paratra ca bhavataḥ śrotum icchāmi tan me vistarato vada
english: What gift, O king, bears fruit both in this world and in the next? I wish to hear it from you; tell me that in full detail.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca imam arthaṃ purā pṛṣṭo nārado devadarśanaḥ yad uktavān asau tan me gadataḥ śṛṇu bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: On this very matter Nārada, who beholds the gods, was once questioned; hear from me as I tell what he then declared, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca annam eva praśaṃsanti devāḥ sarṣigaṇāḥ purā lokatantraṃ hi yajñāś ca sarvam anne pratiṣṭhitam
english: Nārada said: It is food above all that the gods, together with the hosts of sages, praised of old; for the order of the world and the sacrifices—all rest upon food.

sanskrit: annena sadṛśaṃ dānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati tasmād annaṃ viśeṣeṇa dātum icchanti mānavāḥ
english: No gift equal to food has been or shall ever be; therefore men desire above all to give food.

sanskrit: annam ūrjaskaraṃ loke prāṇāś cānne pratiṣṭhitāḥ annena dhāryate sarvaṃ viśvaṃ jagad idaṃ prabho
english: Food gives strength in the world, and the vital breaths are established in food; by food this whole universe is upheld, O lord.

sanskrit: annād gṛhasthā loke 'smin bhikṣavas tata eva ca annāt prabhavati prāṇaḥ pratyakṣaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: From food the householders in this world subsist, and the mendicants likewise; from food springs the breath of life—this is plain to see, and herein is no doubt.

sanskrit: kuṭumbaṃ pīḍayitvāpi brāhmaṇāya mahātmane dātavyaṃ bhikṣave cānnam ātmano bhūtim icchatā
english: Even at the cost of straitening his own household, a man who desires his own welfare should give food to a great-souled brāhmaṇa and to a mendicant.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāyābhirūpāya yo dadyād annam arthine nidadhāti nidhiṃ śreṣṭhaṃ pāralaukikam ātmanaḥ
english: He who gives food to a worthy brāhmaṇa in need lays up for himself the finest of treasures, a treasure for the world beyond.

sanskrit: śrāntam adhvani vartantaṃ vṛddham arham upasthitam arcayed bhūtim anvicchan gṛhastho gṛham āgatam
english: The householder who desires prosperity should honor the weary traveler on the road, the aged and worthy man who has come to his door.

sanskrit: krodham utpatitaṃ hitvā suśīlo vītamatsaraḥ annadaḥ prāpnute rājan divi ceha ca yat sukham
english: Casting off rising anger, well-conducted and free from grudging, the giver of food attains, O king, whatever happiness there is both in heaven and here.

sanskrit: nāvamanyed abhigataṃ na praṇudyāt kathaṃ cana api śvapāke śuni vā na dānaṃ vipraṇaśyati
english: Let him never slight one who has come, nor turn him away by any means; even when given to an outcaste or to a dog, a gift is never lost.

sanskrit: yo dadyād aparikliṣṭam annam adhvani vartate śrāntāyādṛṣṭapūrvāya sa mahad dharmam āpnuyāt
english: He who ungrudgingly gives food to a weary man upon the road, one never seen before, attains a great measure of dharma.

sanskrit: pitṝn devān ṛṣīn viprān atithīṃś ca janādhipa yo naraḥ prīṇayaty annais tasya puṇyaphalaṃ mahat
english: The man who gratifies with food the ancestors, the gods, the sages, the brāhmaṇas, and his guests, O ruler of men—great is the fruit of his merit.

sanskrit: kṛtvāpi pāpakaṃ karma yo dadyād annam arthine brāhmaṇāya viśeṣeṇa na sa pāpena yujyate
english: Even one who has done an evil deed, if he gives food to a needy man—and above all to a brāhmaṇa—is not bound by his sin.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇeṣv akṣayaṃ dānam annaṃ śūdre mahāphalam annadānaṃ ca śūdre ca brāhmaṇe ca viśiṣyate
english: A gift to brāhmaṇas is imperishable; food given to a śūdra bears great fruit; the giving of food, whether to a śūdra or to a brāhmaṇa, is preeminent.

sanskrit: na pṛcched gotracaraṇaṃ svādhyāyaṃ deśam eva vā bhikṣito brāhmaṇeneha janma vānnaṃ prayācitaḥ
english: When food is begged of him here by a brāhmaṇa, let him not inquire into the lineage, the conduct, the sacred study, the homeland, or the birth of the one who asks.

sanskrit: annadasyānnavṛkṣāś ca sarvakāmaphalānvitāḥ bhavantīhātha vāmutra nṛpate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: For the giver of food there grow trees of food laden with the fruit of every desire, whether here or in the world beyond, O king; herein is no doubt.

sanskrit: āśaṃsante hi pitaraḥ suvṛṣṭim iva karṣakāḥ asmākam api putro vā pautro vānnaṃ pradāsyati
english: For the ancestors yearn, as farmers yearn for good rain: 'Will our son too, or our grandson, give food on our behalf?'

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo hi mahad bhūtaṃ svayaṃ dehīti yācate akāmo vā sakāmo vā dattvā puṇyam avāpnuyāt
english: For the brāhmaṇa is a great being who himself begs, saying 'Give'; and whether one gives unwillingly or willingly, by giving one attains merit.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaḥ sarvabhūtānām atithiḥ prasṛtāgrabhuk viprā yam abhigacchanti bhikṣamāṇā gṛhaṃ sadā
english: The brāhmaṇa is the guest of all beings, the one who eats the first portion offered; he it is to whose house the twice-born come ever, begging alms.

sanskrit: satkṛtāś ca nivartante tad atīva pravardhate mahābhoge kule janma pretya prāpnoti bhārata
english: And when they depart honored, that household prospers exceedingly; and after death one attains birth in a family of great abundance, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: dattvā tv annaṃ naro loke tathā sthānam anuttamam mṛṣṭamṛṣṭānnadāyī tu svarge vasati satkṛtaḥ
english: Having given food, a man attains in this world an unsurpassed station; and he who gives the most delicate of foods dwells honored in heaven.
